meta.source: Bambu Lab Wiki P1 Maintenance Recommendations + Bellingham Makerspace Guide

tasks.name: Clean X-axis carbon rods
tasks.summary: Wipe carbon rods with IPA to remove filament dust and debris.
tasks.interval_note: Every 5 spools if printing ABS, ASA, or other volatile filaments
steps: Power off the printer and let it cool completely.
Apply a generous amount of IPA to a clean lint-free cloth or paper towel.
Gently wipe along the full length of each X-axis carbon rod, removing dust and debris.
Use a dry cloth to wipe off any remaining IPA.
Do NOT apply any grease or oil to carbon rods. Grease causes additional buildup and premature wear.
After cleaning, power on and run a homing cycle to confirm smooth movement.
warnings: Never use grease or lubricating oil on carbon rods. Use IPA only.

tasks.name: Lubricate Z-axis lead screws
tasks.summary: Apply grease to the three Z-axis lead screws to ensure smooth vertical movement.
tasks.interval_note: Every 3 months under normal use; more frequently in a high-use environment
symptoms_if_skipped: HMS motor errors on Z axis
consumables: Lubricating grease (Super Lube 92003, Lucas Oil 10533, or Bambu Lab grease)
steps: Home the printer so the bed is at the top position.
Apply a thin coat of lubricating grease to all three lead screws.
Move the bed to its lowest position using the printer menu.
Apply another thin coat of grease to the exposed upper sections of the lead screws.
Home the printer again and repeat the up/down movement 3-5 times to distribute the grease evenly.
Wipe off any excess grease that builds up near the lead screw nuts with a lint-free cloth.
warnings: Do not use grease on the belts. Grease on belts causes slipping and layer shifts.
Do not use grease on X-axis carbon rods.

tasks.name: Lubricate Y-axis linear rods and bearings
tasks.summary: Apply lubricating oil to the Y-axis 8mm linear rods and LMU8 bearings.
tasks.interval_note: Every 3 months, or sooner if you hear grinding or unusual noise from the bed movement
symptoms_if_skipped: Grinding or squeaking from bed during Y movement
Increased resistance when moving bed by hand
consumables: Lubricating oil (Super Lube 52004 or Bambu Lab lubricant oil)
steps: Power off the printer.
Apply 1-2 drops of lubricating oil every 5cm along both Y-axis linear rods.
Avoid over-applying: excess oil attracts dust and drips.
Move the bed back and forth manually several times to distribute oil into the bearings.
If you hear clicking or ball noise from a bearing, apply a small amount of grease to the bearing and work it in by sliding the bearing back and forth.
Wipe off any excess oil from the ends of the rods with a lint-free cloth.
warnings: Do not use grease on the linear rods if lubricant oil is recommended for your model. Check your specific printer's wiki.

tasks.name: Lubricate idler pulleys
tasks.summary: Apply a small amount of lubricating oil between the idler flange and plastic holder to prevent squeaking.
tasks.interval_note: Only when squeaking noises are present during print head movement. Do not lubricate proactively to avoid dust buildup.
symptoms_if_skipped: Squeaking or squealing during X/Y movement
steps: Identify which idler is making noise by listening carefully during a movement.
Apply a very small amount of lubricating oil between the idler flange and the plastic holder, both on top and bottom.
Do NOT apply oil to the belt surface itself.
Run a few movement cycles and listen to confirm the noise is gone.
Wipe any excess oil that may have spread to the belt.
warnings: Only lubricate idlers when squeaking is present. Unnecessary lubrication attracts dust.
Never apply any lubricant directly to the timing belts.

tasks.name: Clean extruder gear (yellow gear)
tasks.summary: Remove filament dust from the extruder drive gear to prevent feed issues.
tasks.interval_note: Every 5 spools for standard filaments (PLA, PETG). Every 2 spools when printing carbon fiber or abrasive filaments.
steps: Heat the nozzle to printing temperature and unload filament completely.
Power off the printer.
Use compressed air to blow into the extruder area around the yellow gear to dislodge dust.
Alternatively, remove the hotend and blow compressed air from underneath the extruder.
Use a stiff brush to remove any remaining compacted filament dust from the gear teeth.
If visible dust persists after using compressed air, the extruder may need disassembly for deeper cleaning. See the Extruder Maintenance Guide.
Reload filament and confirm smooth feeding before printing.
warnings: Compressed air can push debris deeper if aimed incorrectly. Aim to blow debris outward.

tasks.name: Cold pull (hotend cleaning)
tasks.summary: Perform a cold pull to clear residue and debris from inside the nozzle and hotend.
tasks.interval_note: When switching filament types (e.g. ABS to PLA), when under-extrusion is suspected, or after a clog
consumables: PLA filament (preferred for cold pulls due to its properties)
steps: Heat the nozzle to the printing temperature of the filament currently loaded (or 200-220°C for PLA).
Manually push filament through until fresh material comes out cleanly.
Reduce nozzle temperature to 90-100°C for PLA (or the cold-pull temperature for your filament).
While the nozzle cools, maintain gentle forward pressure on the filament.
When the target temperature is reached, firmly and steadily pull the filament straight out.
Inspect the tip: it should be shaped like the inside of the nozzle and show any debris pulled out.
Repeat 2-3 times until the pulled tip comes out clean.
Re-heat to printing temperature and load filament normally before printing.
warnings: Do not attempt to pull filament when the nozzle is fully cool. This can damage the nozzle or PTFE liner.

tasks.name: Clean nozzle exterior and heater block
tasks.summary: Wipe filament buildup off the outside of the nozzle and heater block.
tasks.interval_note: Every 5 spools for standard filaments; every 2 spools for abrasive or high-temp materials
symptoms_if_skipped: Carbonized filament buildup causing thermal readings to drift
tools_needed: Paper towel or brass wire brush
steps: Heat the nozzle to printing temperature (around 200-250°C depending on material).
Put on heat-resistant gloves.
Carefully wipe the outside of the nozzle and heater block with a paper towel or brass wire brush to remove accumulated burnt filament.
Check that the silicone sock is present and undamaged. Replace it if it is torn, missing, or heavily degraded.
Allow to cool before any further inspection.
warnings: Nozzle temperature can exceed 250°C. Always wear gloves.
Do not use steel tools that could scratch the nozzle surface or damage the heater block coating.

tasks.name: Replace hotend silicone sock
tasks.summary: Replace the silicone sock that insulates the heater block when worn or missing.
tasks.interval_note: Replace when the sock is torn, missing, or has significant filament ingrained into it
symptoms_if_skipped: Increased risk of heater block burns
consumables: Bambu Lab P1S/P1P silicone sock (or compatible third-party replacement)
steps: Heat the nozzle to printing temperature to soften any adhered filament on the sock.
Allow to cool to room temperature.
Gently peel off the old silicone sock from the heater block.
Clean any residual filament from the heater block surface.
Slide the new silicone sock onto the heater block, ensuring all faces are covered.
Heat the nozzle to confirm the sock seats properly and does not fall off.
warnings: Remove the sock only when the heater block is at room temperature to avoid burns.

tasks.name: Replace nozzle
tasks.summary: Replace a worn, clogged, or damaged nozzle with a fresh one.
tasks.interval_note: Brass nozzles: every 3-6 months of regular printing, or sooner with abrasive filaments. Hardened steel: every 6-12 months.
symptoms_if_skipped: Nozzle orifice visibly enlarged or irregular
tools_needed: Wrench or nozzle socket for P1S (refer to Bambu guide)
consumables: Replacement nozzle (0.4mm brass or hardened steel as appropriate)
steps: Heat the nozzle to 250°C to soften any bonded filament.
Unload filament completely.
Put on heat-resistant gloves.
Use the correct wrench to remove the old nozzle while holding the heater block steady.
Thread the new nozzle in by hand first, then tighten with the wrench while the block is still hot.
Do not over-tighten: snug plus a small fraction of a turn is sufficient.
Allow to cool and perform a test print to verify no leaks around the nozzle.
warnings: Always change nozzles at temperature to avoid stripping threads.
Hold the heater block with a second wrench or pliers to avoid twisting the heater wires.

tasks.name: Inspect and replace PTFE tube couplers
tasks.summary: Check pneumatic PTFE tube fittings for damage and replace if filament cannot seat securely.
tasks.interval_note: Inspect every 3 months; replace immediately if filament cannot be secured or cannot pass through
symptoms_if_skipped: Filament not feeding smoothly into extruder
PTFE tube pulling out during retraction
Unexpected filament jams in the buffer
consumables: PTFE tube couplers (pneumatic connectors) for P1 series
steps: Unload filament and power off the printer.
Inspect the PTFE tube coupler at the extruder: insert and pull filament by hand to confirm it seats and releases properly.
Check the coupler at the AMS buffer for the same.
Look for cracks, deformation, or internal damage by shining a flashlight into the fitting.
If the tube cannot be secured or filament cannot pass cleanly, the coupler must be replaced.
Follow the Bambu wiki guide for your specific coupler replacement procedure.

tasks.name: Replace activated carbon air filter
tasks.summary: Replace the internal air filter to maintain VOC and particle filtration (P1S enclosed printer).
tasks.interval_note: Every 3 months at approximately 8 hours/day of printing; sooner when printing ABS, ASA, or other high-VOC materials
symptoms_if_skipped: Reduced effectiveness of enclosure for ABS/ASA
consumables: Bambu Lab activated carbon air filter for P1S
steps: Power off the printer.
Locate the air filter cover on the side of the P1S enclosure.
Open the cover using the release clip.
Remove the old filter by pulling it out using the top and bottom handles.
Insert the new filter and close the cover until it clicks.
Note the replacement date for future reference.
warnings: P1P does not have an enclosure air filter. This task applies to P1S only.

tasks.name: Check and adjust belt tension
tasks.summary: Verify X and Y belt tension is correct to prevent layer shifting and ringing artifacts.
tasks.interval_note: Check monthly; re-tension if layer shifts or ringing appear
steps: Power off the printer.
Gently pluck each belt as you would a guitar string. They should emit a consistent, moderately high-pitched tone.
A belt that is too loose will sound low and feel slack; a belt that is too tight may feel stiff to move and can stress the motors.
If adjustment is needed, locate the belt tensioner for the axis and turn it clockwise to tighten.
After adjusting, run a vibration compensation calibration from the printer menu.
Print a ringing test object (available in OrcaSlicer calibrations) to verify the fix.
warnings: Do not over-tighten. Excessive belt tension stresses motor bearings and reduces motor lifespan.

tasks.name: Clean internal camera lens
tasks.summary: Wipe the internal camera lens to maintain first-layer inspection and timelapse clarity.
tasks.interval_note: Monthly, or when camera feed appears blurry or cloudy
tools_needed: Microfiber cloth or lens cleaning wipe
steps: Power off the printer.
Locate the internal camera (top front of the enclosure on P1S).
Gently wipe the lens surface with a dry microfiber cloth or lens cleaning wipe.
Do not use liquids or abrasive cloths.
Power on and check the camera feed from Bambu Handy or OrcaSlicer to confirm clarity.

tasks.name: Full calibration run
tasks.summary: Run a complete calibration sequence after maintenance or when print quality degrades.
tasks.interval_note: After any maintenance that touches motion components, or when print quality unexpectedly changes
consumables: Small amount of filament for calibration prints
steps: On the printer screen, navigate to Settings > Calibration.
Run 'Calibration All' which performs vibration compensation, motor noise cancellation, and auto bed leveling.
Alternatively run individual calibrations: Bed Leveling, then Vibration Compensation.
After calibration, print a small test object to confirm results.
If using OrcaSlicer's calibration tools, run flow rate and pressure advance calibration for any new filament spools.

tasks.name: Clean AMS filament channels
tasks.summary: Remove filament fragments and dust from AMS slots and the buffer tube.
tasks.interval_note: Monthly, or after any clog or broken filament event inside the AMS
steps: Remove all spools from the AMS.
Shine a flashlight into each slot to look for filament fragments.
Use tweezers to remove any visible pieces.
Use compressed air to blow through each channel from the spool end outward.
Inspect the buffer tube for any debris.
Reload spools and test loading/unloading each slot before printing.
warnings: Do not use metal objects that could scratch the RFID sensors or filament guides.

tasks.name: Inspect AMS filament cutter
tasks.summary: Check the AMS cutter blade for dullness or debris that could cause cut failures.
tasks.interval_note: Every 3 months, or when cutter HMS errors appear
symptoms_if_skipped: Filament not cutting cleanly during tool changes
steps: Power off the printer.
Open the AMS side cover following the AMS maintenance guide.
Visually inspect the cutter blade for debris, filament chips, or visible dullness.
Clear any debris carefully with tweezers.
Manually actuate the cutter handle to confirm it moves freely through its full range.
If the blade is visibly worn or the cutter consistently fails, order a replacement blade assembly.
Close the cover and run a test print with a tool change to verify operation.
warnings: The cutter blade is sharp. Handle with care and follow AMS safety notes.

tasks.name: Clear dust from toolhead fans
tasks.summary: Remove dust accumulation from part cooling and hotend fans to maintain airflow.
tasks.interval_note: Every 3 months, or when fan noise changes or HMS fan speed warnings appear
steps: Power off the printer and disconnect power.
Use compressed air to blow through the fan grille of the part cooling fan and hotend fan.
Use tweezers to carefully remove any large filament strands caught in the fan blades.
Spin each fan blade by hand to confirm it rotates freely.
Power on, heat the nozzle briefly, and listen to confirm both fans spin without noise or wobble.
warnings: Disconnect power before working near the fans. Fan blades can cause cuts if spinning.

tasks.name: Clean build plate surface
tasks.summary: Clean the PEI or textured plate with IPA to restore adhesion.
tasks.interval_note: Before every few prints, or whenever adhesion unexpectedly decreases
symptoms_if_skipped: Parts not sticking to the bed
tools_needed: Clean paper towels or lint-free cloth
steps: Allow the bed to cool to room temperature.
Spray or pour a small amount of IPA onto the build plate.
Wipe with a clean paper towel in one direction to lift oils and residue.
Repeat with a fresh paper towel until no residue is visible.
Allow the IPA to fully evaporate before printing.
Do not touch the cleaned surface with bare hands; oils from skin will reduce adhesion.
warnings: Do not use acetone on PEI plates. Acetone damages the PEI coating.
For stubborn residue (glue stick, hairspray), warm water and a small amount of dish soap can be used, followed by an IPA wipe.
